Okay, I need to explain why the sky is blue during the day and red at sunset using Rayleigh scattering. Let me recall what Rayleigh scattering is. It’s the scattering of light by particles much smaller than the wavelength of the light, like molecules in the atmosphere. 

During the day, sunlight travels through a shorter path in the atmosphere compared to sunset. Shorter path means less scattering. Blue light has a shorter wavelength, so it scatters more. That ’s why the sky appears blue. 

At sunset, the sun is lower, so the light has to pass through more atmosphere. The blue light gets scattered away, leaving longer wavelengths like red and orange. These longer wavelengths scatter less, so they dominate the color we see.

final_answer:
The sky appears blue during the day due to Rayleigh scattering, where shorter wavelengths (blue/violet) scatter more efficiently than longer ones (red/orange). This scattering occurs because the intensity of scattered light is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the wavelength (I ∝ 1/λ⁴), making blue light (λ ≈ 400 nm) scatter about 9 times more than red light (λ ≈ 700 nm). As sunlight passes through the atmosphere, blue light is scattered in all directions, filling the sky with blue hues. 

At sunset, sunlight travels through a longer atmospheric path, increasing scattering. Most blue light is scattered away, leaving predominantly red/orange wavelengths (which scatter less) to reach the observer. This effect, combined with the sun’s lower angle, results in the reddish appearance of the sky during sunrise/sunset.
